# Nonzero centroid midpoint defects with zero endpoint enlargement reserve
assert an OC counterexample or local depth minimality.

The reserve \({\cal R}_p\) is defined and proved exact in
candidate be4d9f84e764ef2a:
a monotone enlargement \(L_p\supset K_p\), with every other fiber
fixed, is actual if and only if \(L_p\subset{\cal R}_p\).

These examples show that nonzero centroid midpoint defect can coexist
with
\[
                 {\cal R}_0=K_0,\qquad {\cal R}_2=K_2.    \tag{1}
\]
The first defect is entirely nonadditivity of the centroid of a
Minkowski midpoint. The second defect is entirely due to *strict
inclusion surplus* beyond a Minkowski midpoint. Thus neither kind
of centroid defect alone forces an independently enlargeable endpoint.

## 1. Actual three-fiber realization and the relevant support test

Place positive bodies \(K_0,K_1,K_2\) at integer bases \(0,1,2\),
with \(A=(K_0+K_2)/2\subset K_1\), and take their convex hull.
The endpoint fibers are exactly their specified bodies, since
the endpoints are extreme bases. A convex combination at base 1,
after canceling any contribution already at 1, is an equal
combination of bases 0 and 2. Its continuous part lies in
\(A\subset K_1\). The middle fiber is therefore exactly \(K_1\).
The projection is \([0,2]\), so these are all integer fibers.

If for every facet normal \(r\) of \(K_0\),
\[
                    h_{K_1}(r)=h_A(r),                  \tag{2}
\]
then no proper monotone enlargement of \(K_0\) is compatible with
fixed \(K_1,K_2\). Indeed feasibility of \(L_0\) implies
\[
 h_{L_0}(r)\le2h_{K_1}(r)-h_{K_2}(r)=h_{K_0}(r).
 \]
All facet inequalities of \(K_0\) hold on \(L_0\), forcing
\(L_0\subset K_0\). The same assertion holds for \(K_2\).
It is enough to preserve these finitely many support values;
one need not have \(K_1=A\).

## 2. A planar defect caused solely by Minkowski-centroid nonadditivity

Let
\[
 T=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\},\quad
 Q=[0,1]^2,
\]
and use
\[
 K_0=T,\quad K_2=Q,\quad
 K_1=A=\frac{T+Q}{2}
   =\{0\le x,y\le1,\ x+y\le3/2\}.                       \tag{3}
\]
For the Minkowski equality, the sum \(T+Q\) is contained in
\(\{0\le x,y\le2,\ x+y\le3\}\); every vertex of that pentagon,
\[
 (0,0),(2,0),(2,1),(1,2),(0,2),
\]
is explicitly the sum of a vertex of \(T\) and a vertex of \(Q\).
This proves (3). The ambient body can also be written directly as
\[
 0\le z\le2,\quad 0\le x,y\le1,\quad x+y\le1+z/2.         \tag{4}
\]
Its fibers at intermediate real \(z\) are the corresponding
Minkowski interpolates, as is checked at their five vertices.

The middle pentagon removes from the unit square a right triangle
of area \(1/8\), with centroid \((5/6,5/6)\). Thus
\[
 |K_0|=\frac12,\quad |K_1|=\frac78,\quad |K_2|=1,
 \qquad M=\frac{19}{8}.
\]
The base has \(k=2\) occupied parities and
\[
       \max_p|K_p|=1<\frac{M}{k}=\frac{19}{16}.          \tag{5}
\]
This is strictly outside the heavy-fiber sufficient case.

The three centroids are
\[
 g_0=(1/3,1/3),\quad g_2=(1/2,1/2),\quad
 g_1=(19/42,19/42).
\]
Indeed the middle first coordinate moment is
\(1/2-(1/8)(5/6)=19/48\), and division by \(7/8\)
gives \(19/42\). Therefore
\[
          g_1-\frac{g_0+g_2}{2}=(1/28,1/28)\ne0.       \tag{6}
\]
There is no target inclusion surplus: \(K_1=A\) exactly.
All support inequalities for the midpoint are equalities,
so Section 1 gives (1) for both endpoints.

This also has a positive Brunn--Minkowski root deficit, since
the positive bodies \(T,Q\) are not homothetic. The deficit is
shape information; it supplies no endpoint support reserve.

## 3. A spatial defect caused solely by strict inclusion surplus

Use centered bodies so that all original Minkowski-centroid
terms vanish. Let \(t=1/10\), let \(K_0=[-1/2,1/2]^3\), and
let \(K_2=B K_0\), where \(B\) has columns
\[
 g_4=(1,t,0),\qquad g_5=(0,1,t),\qquad g_6=(t,0,1).
\]
Also put \(g_1=e_1,g_2=e_2,g_3=e_3\). The determinant of
\(B\) is \(1+t^3=1001/1000>0\). The Minkowski midpoint is
the centrally symmetric zonotope
\[
 A=\frac{K_0+K_2}{2}
     =\sum_{i=1}^6[-1/4,1/4]g_i.                       \tag{7}
\]
In particular \(g_{K_0}=g_{K_2}=g_A=0\).

Set
\[
 u=(0,-1/10,1),\quad
 c=(-9/40,-11/40,1/2),\quad
 \varepsilon=1/1000,\quad
 v=c+\varepsilon u=(-9/40,-2751/10000,501/1000),
\]
and define
\[
                            K_1=\operatorname{conv}(A,v).         \tag{8}
\]

### 3.1 Complete facet verification

For any nonzero \(r\),
\[
                       h_A(r)=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^6|r\cdot g_i|.   \tag{9}
\]
The face of \(A\) exposed by \(r\) has direction space
spanned by those \(g_i\) with \(r\cdot g_i=0\): in (7),
the nonzero scalar products fix the respective endpoint,
while zero scalar products leave their whole segment free.
Thus every facet normal is parallel to
\(r_{ij}=g_i\times g_j\) for some independent pair.
Conversely every nonzero such cross product exposes a facet.
The two signs of these fifteen cross products therefore
include every facet, with harmless repetitions.

Here is a complete rational support certificate. The entry
is \(10^6(h_A(r_{ij})-|r_{ij}\cdot v|)\):

| pair \(ij\) | scaled slack | pair \(ij\) | scaled slack | pair \(ij\) | scaled slack |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
| 12 | 24000 | 13 | 249900 | 14 | 2400 |
| 15 | -1010 | 16 | 249900 | 23 | 300000 |
| 24 | 24000 | 25 | 30000 | 26 | 252400 |
| 34 | 274900 | 35 | 300000 | 36 | 24990 |
| 45 | 1490 | 46 | 280160 | 56 | 249899 |

Each entry follows directly from the six displayed rational
generators and (9). For the sole negative entry \(r_{15}=u\),
\[
 u\cdot v=h_A(u)+101/100000>h_A(u).
 \]
Hence \(v\) violates exactly the positive \(u\)-facet of \(A\)
and strictly satisfies every other facet inequality.

The \(u\)-facet itself is
\[
 F=c+[-1/4,1/4]g_1+[-1/4,1/4]g_5.                     \tag{10}
\]
Indeed \(u\cdot g_1=u\cdot g_5=0\), and the other four
scalar products have signs minus, plus, minus, plus
at indices \(2,3,4,6\). Their fixed endpoints sum to \(c\).
It is a parallelogram with centroid \(c\).

### 3.2 Strict added volume and an exact nonzero centroid

Because \(v\) violates only the facet \(F\), the added region
is exactly the pyramid from \(F\) to \(v\), up to its boundary.
To see this, any segment from \(v\) to a point of \(A\)
satisfies all the other facet inequalities throughout. Its
first point in \(A\) is therefore on \(F\). Conversely every
point of the open pyramid lies beyond that facet and
satisfies the other inequalities.

The sides of the base parallelogram are \(g_1/2,g_5/2\).
Its pyramid volume is consequently
\[
 \Delta=\frac13\left|
       \det(g_1/2,g_5/2,\varepsilon u)\right|
        =\frac{\varepsilon(1+t^2)}{12}
        =\frac{101}{1200000}>0.                        \tag{11}
\]
Its centroid is
\[
 g_{\rm add}=\frac{3c+v}{4}
       =c+\frac{\varepsilon u}{4}
       =(-9/40,-11001/40000,2001/4000).                \tag{12}
\]
The factor \(1/4\) follows by integrating the squared
linear section scale of a three-dimensional pyramid.
In particular
\[
 u\cdot g_{\rm add}=\frac{211101}{400000}>0.            \tag{13}
\]

For completeness the exact zonotope volume is
\[
 |A|=\frac18\sum_{i<j<l}
              |\det(g_i,g_j,g_l)|=\frac{8631}{8000}.   \tag{14}
\]
The determinant numerators, multiplied by 1000 in
lexicographic triple order, are
\[
 1000,0,100,1000,100,1000,0,10,100,1000,
 1000,0,100,100,1000,10,1000,10,100,1001.
\]
Their sum is 8631. The zonotope formula has an elementary
proof: adding a segment \([0,w]\) to a convex body increases
volume by \(|w|\) times its orthogonal projection area onto
\(w^\perp\), since each parallel interval fiber has its
length increased by \(|w|\). Induct on the number of
segments and on dimension, starting with interval length.
The projection-area terms are precisely the determinants
containing the new segment. Applied to the translated
segments \([0,g_i/2]\), this gives (14).

Combining the zero centroid of \(A\) with (11)--(14) gives
\[
 |K_1|=\frac{1294751}{1200000},\qquad
 g_1=\frac{101}{1294751}
       (-9/40,-11001/40000,2001/4000)\ne0.             \tag{15}
\]
The endpoint centroids and \(g_A\) are all zero. Thus the
entire nonzero midpoint centroid defect \(g_1-(g_0+g_2)/2\)
comes from *target inclusion surplus*, not from any
nonadditivity of \(g_A\).

### 3.3 Both endpoints nevertheless have zero reserve

The facet normals of \(K_0\) are the two signs of the
cross products within \(\{g_1,g_2,g_3\}\). Those of \(K_2\)
are the two signs of the cross products within
\(\{g_4,g_5,g_6\}\). Every corresponding support slack
in the table is strictly positive. Therefore the added
point \(v\) changes none of these support values:
\[
 h_{K_1}(r)=h_A(r)
 \quad\hbox{for every facet normal of either endpoint}.
 \]
The support test in Section 1 now proves exactly
\({\cal R}_0=K_0\) and \({\cal R}_2=K_2\).
The only relaxed facet normal is created by a pair of
edges from *different* endpoint bodies.

### 3.4 No heavy fiber

All three masses are positive and exact:
\[
 |K_0|=1,\quad |K_2|=\frac{1001}{1000},\quad
 |K_1|=\frac{1294751}{1200000},\quad
 M=\frac{3695951}{1200000}.
 \]
The largest is \(|K_1|\), and
\[
 2\cdot1294751=2589502<3695951.
 \]
Thus every fiber has mass strictly less than \(M/2=M/k\).
This second obstruction also lies outside the heavy-fiber
sufficient case.

## 4. Dimension padding and scope

Take the Cartesian product of every continuous fiber with
the same centered unit cube. This preserves all volumes,
the displayed nonzero centroid coordinates, and the
midpoint inclusions. The locked endpoint facet inequalities
still force the original endpoint in the old coordinates,
and unchanged upper and lower coordinate faces force
the same unit cube in the new coordinates. Consequently
the planar example extends to every \(d\ge2\), and the
strict-inclusion example to every \(d\ge3\).

For every \(n\ge1\), take the Cartesian product of the
ambient body with the binary integer box \([0,1]^{n-1}\).
The base has \(3\cdot2^{n-1}\) points and exactly \(2^n\)
occupied parity classes. Anchored combinations at a binary
vertex cannot leave its binary layer, so endpoint reserve
remains locked in every column. Total mass is multiplied
by \(2^{n-1}\), while \(M/k\) remains one half of the
single-column mass. The strict no-heavy inequalities
are therefore unchanged.

These are counterexamples to inferring independent
endpoint enlargement reserve from a positive midpoint
centroid defect, even after separating the two sources
of that defect. They do not exclude joint endpoint and
middle changes, signed shape changes, or descent by
other mechanisms. No critical-cap stress or local
minimum is asserted for either example.

The exact verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_zero_endpoint_reserve_centroid_defects_coherent.py
checks the planar moments and facets, all spatial
cross-product slacks, the twenty determinant terms,
the added-pyramid moment, both endpoint support locks,
and the strict no-heavy inequalities. These computations
certify the displayed rational identities; the proofs
of completeness and actual compatibility are above.
